text:
ashwin: FYI I spun up a canary for Hushard17B with int4-dynamic-symmetric quant. Seeing OOMs and lots of memory fragmentation on hx-rt nodes right after first multi-turns.

ashwin: relevant log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18 21:03:12] oom: failed to allocate 2.1GB for KV cache op
[2026-03-18 21:03:12] mem: RSS spike 82GB -> 128GB in 400ms
[2026-03-18 21:03:12] evict: attempted 0 slots, reserved 0
```

maya: ouch. what were the canary defaults (batching / max_new_tokens / kv_prefetch)?

ashwin: current canary config:
```
quant: int4-dynamic-symmetric
batch_size: 8
batching.window_ms: 30
batching.max_tokens_per_batch: 8192
max_new_tokens: 512
kv_prefetch: true
reserve_slots: 0
```

liam: first idea: lower concurrency and max_new_tokens. On similar 17B we fixed frag by dropping max_new_tokens to 160-192 and batch_size -> 4. Also disable kv_prefetch for canary.

ashwin: noted. will try batch_size=4 and max_new_tokens=192, kv_prefetch=false. any other low-risk knobs?

sophia: add reserve_slots: 12 and enable slot_compaction: true (not default for Hushard yet). Also set eviction_policy: conservative so we don't spike allocation trying to keep KV for long contexts.

maya: for quality: int4 dropped rouge on our summarization eval by ~2.6 vs fp16. If we reduce max_new_tokens the generation distribution changes; need to re-run evals with the new defaults to confirm regression still exists.

ashwin: running quick A/B: fp16 vs int4-v2 with new settings. small eval harness across 200 summarization prompts, seed fixed. will post numbers in ~30m.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary/hushard17b/int4-v2 at 2460012400 by ashwin

liam: additional tuning suggestions we used before:
- batching.window_ms: 15 (pacer)
- batching.max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
- soft_batching: true (avoid large spikes)
- max_new_tokens_default: 192
- kv_eviction_window: 8

ashwin: quick results after 3 runs with new config (batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=192, kv_prefetch=false, reserve_slots=12): no OOMs, RSS stabilized around 88-92GB, fragmentation indicators dropped (fewer mmap churn logs). Quality: rouge delta improved to -1.2 (int4 vs fp16).

sophia: good improvement. once you confirm across longer runs (1k requests) we should push the defaults for Hushard17B canary and open a follow-up RFC to make per-model defaults documented in model-catalog.

maya: also add a regression alert: if rouge delta > 2 for a 200-sample eval then auto-fallback to fp16 for that model in hosted pool.

ashwin: will run extended canary overnight, then update #model-onboard board with metrics. thanks all :thumbsup:

ashwin: quick note for release engineers: if int4 quality doesn't converge, plan is to keep int8 canary image ready; it has slightly higher cost but no regression in our tests so far.

sophia: filed follow-up ticket: MH-4523 (per-model default knobs + compaction + regression alert).

ashwin: closing thread for now, will post final canary summary tomorrow.
